references.text: Moses' song of praise declares that the LORD is exalted above all gods, reflecting Jethro's confession of God's greatness
The LORD is described as the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God
The LORD is a great God and a great king above all gods
The LORD is supreme over all the earth, highly exalted above all gods
The psalmist confesses that the LORD is great and that our Lord is above all gods
The Egyptians acted deceitfully toward the Israelites, showing how they 'zadu' (acted arrogantly) against them
The downfall of Egypt in the Red Sea shows how God judged them for their arrogant plans against Israel
The Levites confess that the Egyptians acted arrogantly toward the Israelites, and God displayed His power
Uses the same word 'zadu' (acted arrogantly) regarding the ancestors' rebellion against God
1 Chronicles 16:25 repeats Jethro's confession as part of the public song of praise about God's saving acts.
Psalm 96:4 carries forward Jethro's confession as a central element in Israel's liturgical expression of faith.
Psalm 47:3 expands Jethro's specific observation about Egypt into a general truth about God's rule over all the earth.
Solomon uses exactly the same confession as Jethro to justify the building of the temple.
